answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust grow like an orchard: every identity starts as a seedling in a shared garden with capped earnings, and standing rises only through verified useful work attested by established peers. Each attestation is a whisper of trust passed from one real contributor to another, never self-issued. A farm of a thousand fakes must therefore do a thousand identities' worth of real, checked work over many epochs before any of them can earn, so the cost of the attack equals the cost of honestly participating at scale.
